A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Volume Transformer study and are readable throughout, including equations, tables, figures, references, and trailing qualitative-result pages. Neither contains a separately labeled appendix. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Volt segmentation results, efficiency measurements, training analyses, and architectural ablations in Tables 1–5 and Figures 1–6.

after.justification: V2 retains original Volt experiments and additionally reports ScanNet++ instance-segmentation and SceneFun3D functionality-segmentation results.

M1.justification: Patch tokenization, global attention, 3D RoPE, prediction heads, and the distillation objective remain unchanged. V2 documents linear projection and voxel shuffling as an equivalent implementation of the existing decoder, rather than introducing a different model component.

E1.justification: V2 adds SceneFun3D functionality segmentation, requiring identification of small interactive-part instances and their affordance labels across nine categories. This substantially extends task coverage beyond conventional semantic and instance segmentation. It also adds ScanNet++ instance evaluation; v1 evaluated that dataset only for semantic segmentation.

E2.justification: The new SceneFun3D comparison evaluates LERF, OpenTrack3D, and Mask3D-F against Volt-B in Table 4. Existing comparisons retain their methods. The additional ScanNet++ instance column extends already included SPFormer, OneFormer3D, and SGIFormer comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 introduces SceneFun3D test evaluation using AP, AP50, and AP25 and describes its released 200/30/85 scene splits. It revises reported SemanticKITTI training sequences from 9 to 10, ARKit LabelMaker classes from 184 to 185, and Volt-B size from 94.3M to 87.7M parameters. These reporting changes do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Existing ablation evidence receives limited revisions: the reported SemanticKITTI decoder benefit changes from 0.9 to 0.6 mIoU, and patch-size latency measurements change in Table 5. The tested variants, training-recipe analyses, and qualitative examples remain the same; no new robustness or sensitivity study is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. V2 retains the existing single-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds SceneFun3D results, including Volt-B AP/AP50/AP25 of 22.7/34.5/42.6, and ScanNet++ instance results of 54.9 mAP50 versus 43.5, 43.3, and 45.7 for SPFormer, OneFormer3D, and SGIFormer. Existing entries also change: PTv2 ScanNet test mIoU becomes 75.2 instead of 74.2; default SemanticKITTI ablation mIoU becomes 70.5 instead of 70.8; ScanNet200 patch latencies change from 34/14/13 to 67/27/26 ms. Most original headline segmentation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the voxel-count constraint from M<N to M≤N, admitting the case where every point occupies a distinct voxel. The RoPE and distillation equations otherwise retain their mathematical content, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the specific shortcut-learning diagnosis with poor generalization. The introduction revises Volt-B's claimed memory saving from 48% to 38% and extends the instance-segmentation state-of-the-art claim to ScanNet++. The three central architectural, training, and scaling contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: V2 interprets SceneFun3D results as evidence of applicability to fine-grained functional scene understanding. It moderates the shortcut-learning attribution and describes outdoor performance as nearly matching PPT on the third benchmark, consistent with 72.2 versus 72.3 mIoU. Existing explanations of inductive biases, scaling, and overfitting largely remain.

D1.justification: Sections 3–3.2 newly document implementation without sparse-convolution engines: direct linear patch projection and equivalent linear-plus-voxel-shuffle decoding, retaining features at occupied voxels. V1 instead specifies sparse convolution and transposed convolution. The project link and principal training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including SceneFun3D, LERF, OpenTrack3D, PyTorch, LAION-5B, contrastive language-image scaling, and latent diffusion. It removes the Kaplan scaling-law and JFT-related references while retaining the central positioning against specialized 3D backbones. Reference renumbering and duplicate removal do not constitute additional changes.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract and expands the tokenization and decoder explanations, adds a functionality-segmentation paragraph, and makes localized wording and citation-format edits. The section order and overall narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains a ScanNet++ column, and Table 4 pairs the new SceneFun3D results with a condensed positional-encoding ablation. Figures and tables shift with text reflow, and selected captions and legends change. The architecture illustration, plotted trends, and trailing qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the general-purpose-backbone evidence with functionality and additional instance-segmentation evaluations, clarifies an equivalent implementation, and resolves inconsistencies in memory claims, default ablation accuracy, and latency reporting. These improve breadth and clarity without materially changing the central method or established findings. Limited task-specific training detail for the new functionality experiment constrains the reproducibility benefit.
